Influenza vaccination ⁤in Thailand: Protecting High-Risk‍ Groups and the General ⁣Public Influenza,a highly contagious respiratory illness,poses meaningful health risks,notably for vulnerable populations. In thailand, the ​Department of Disease Control has outlined specific guidelines for influenza vaccination, emphasizing the importance of protecting high-risk groups.This article delves into the critical aspects ‌of influenza vaccination, including​ target groups, benefits,⁣ and cost ‍considerations.
High-Risk Groups for Influenza Vaccination The department of ​Disease Control has identified several high-risk groups‍ that ⁤should ‍prioritize getting the influenza vaccine. These groups include:
Pregnant women aged‍ 4 months or more : Pregnancy can weaken the immune system,making expectant mothers more susceptible to influenza complications. Children​ aged 6⁣ months to 2 years : Young children have ​underdeveloped immune systems and are at higher risk of severe illness. Individuals with chronic conditions :⁣ This includes those with chronic lung disease, ‌asthma, ⁤stroke, kidney failure, cancer, and diabetes. People aged 65 years or more : Seniors are​ more likely to experience severe symptoms and⁣ complications from influenza. Thalassemia patients and those⁤ with immune deficiencies : ‍This⁤ includes HIV-infected individuals⁢ with symptoms. Obesity (weight > 100 kilograms or BMI > 35 kg/m²) : Obesity can exacerbate the severity of influenza. People with brain disabilities : Those who cannot self-care⁢ are at higher risk of complications. Benefits and Cost Considerations The influenza vaccine ‍offers numerous benefits, including:
Free of charge for high-risk groups : the government provides free‌ vaccinations ⁤for those who fall into the ⁢high-risk categories. before traveling abroad : For the general public, the vaccine is recommended before international‍ travel to prevent⁢ the spread‍ of influenza. Immunity building : The vaccine acts as an alternative to​ build immunity against influenza strains. Affordable cost : The cost for the influenza vaccine is relatively low, making it accessible⁤ to the general public. For more information, individuals ‍can‍ contact the Department of Disease Control Hotline at⁤ Tel. 1422.
When to Get the Influenza Vaccine The most effective time to ‌get the influenza vaccine is typically in the fall,as it takes about two weeks for the body to develop immunity after vaccination. ⁣This timing aligns with the onset‌ of the influenza season, ensuring maximum protection.
Conclusion Influenza vaccination is a critical measure to prevent the spread and severity ⁤of influenza, particularly ⁣among high-risk groups. By following the guidelines set by the Department of Disease Control,⁢ individuals ⁣can protect themselves and their ‌communities from ‌the potentially severe effects of influenza. For further details and inquiries,contact the Department of Disease Control Hotline at Tel. 1422.
